frames.review_note: Acceptable. The wide courtyard at first light after rain matches the script: the jackfruit tree on a worn stone platform, a mango-wood pyre under the branches, small mourners in white standing back, and the walking stick leaning alone against the trunk. There is no living Padmini and no text. The open sky at top left (about x 0.02-0.40, y 0.03-0.30) holds both captions. Minor: (1) the shrouded body already lies on the pyre, while panel 1.2 shows it still on the bier. This reads as an establishing tableau, but it is a small sequence wrinkle. (2) A tiny hanging glass lantern on the far-right verandah (about x 0.99, y 0.46) breaks the no-glass-lantern rule. Paint it out or retouch it into a brass lamp before placement.

Minor only. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch27 row: Kerala topknot, grey streak at the temple, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold ear stud, bare-chested in a plain borderless white mundu, with no chain, sacred thread or forehead marks. His left forearm hangs with no brand showing. His shoulder cloth is draped over the left shoulder rather than knotted at the waist, as on his sheet. The third bearer's face is hidden behind the bier and only his grey beard shows, so he reads as an elder. The priest matches the V13 face, with ash bands, a red dot, the sacred thread and a gold-bordered angavastram, but his lips are closed rather than visibly moving. The shroud covers the body completely. The courtyard has the ring of floor stones, the jackfruit tree, the wood pyre, the walking stick leaning alone and brass open-wick lamps, so it fits panels 1.1 and 1.5. There is no text, noose, gore or anachronism, and the hands are sound. The long caption can sit in the clear pale sky at top centre and left (about x 0.28 to 0.75, y 0.0 to 0.17), clear of every face.

Acceptable. The beat is right: the priest's hand passes the burning torch and Nagoji's RIGHT hand closes around it below. Both hands are anatomically sound. Nagoji matches: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, grey streak at the temple, warm firelight on his face. His left arm is out of frame. The priest matches the V13 sheet. The background is consistent with 1.4: the body on the pyre and the stick against the trunk. Minor: his hair is half up, a crown knot with curls down the back, which is consistent with 1.5. One soft background lamp under the verandah (about x 0.30, y 0.36) has a glass lantern housing, which is against the bible's no-glass-lantern rule. It is small and out of focus at panel size, but retouch it into an open-wick brass lamp before placement.

Acceptable. Nandini is a small girl of about six with both arms wrapped round a large brass pot against her stomach. Revathi matches her sheet face with grey threading at the temples, plain borderless white, no jasmine, and the tali as her only visible gold; her hand rests on the child's shoulder. The elders behind wear shoulder cloths knotted tight. Nagoji is absent. Hands are sound. The setting matches the neighbouring panels: the shrouded body on the pyre, brass lamps, and the stick against the jackfruit trunk. Place both captions over the roof and sky band top centre to right (about x 0.40-0.78, y 0.02-0.22), clear of Revathi's head. Very minor: Revathi may wear a tiny ear stud.

Acceptable. The pyre is alight with smoke climbing through the jackfruit leaves into a pale sky. Nagoji stands small beside the flames, holding the lowered burning torch in his right hand, and his left forearm is hidden. He matches: Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, moustache, clean chin, bare-chested, plain white mundu. The walking stick leans against the trunk in the left foreground. There is no text and no gore; the shroud only shows among the flames. Place the caption on the low-detail paved floor at bottom right (about x 0.55-0.95, y 0.86-0.98) or in the smoke at upper centre. Minor: the stick is sharp rather than soft-focus, and here the pyre sits on its own rectangular plinth clear of the trunk, slightly unlike 1.1.

Minor: a small brass pot on the desk beside the palm-leaf bundles could be read as an ink pot, and the desk is more table than low desk. Otherwise clean. Nagoji has his topknot, grey at the temples, curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, mundu, shoulder cloth and silver chain, with no coat. His hand guides the stylus over the child's fingers. Nandini is a round-faced child in plain white. The tax collector waits by the steps with his bundle. The plain wall at upper left leaves clear space for both captions.

Minor issues only. Varma's hair knot sits at the crown and back rather than as a side knot above his left ear, and he has no forehead mark here, though he has one in 2.5. The rest is clean: Ramayyan matches his sheet with stylus and palm-leaf bundles. Nagoji is correct (topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain). The map is unlabelled with red, black and brown washes, blue hulls and a narrow green southern tip. The banner emblem has no text, and the upper-left wall and window area is clear for both captions.

Clean. A cream-and-gold arm with a gold bangle and ring points at the small green Travancore tip of an unlabelled map: red to the north, black to the northeast, brown to the east, and blue hulls along the sea. No face is in frame. The room has laterite walls, timber pillars and open shutters, matching the war-hall setting, and the hand anatomy is sound. The plain laterite wall at upper centre and right has room for both Varma balloons. Varma is off-panel to the upper left, where his arm enters.

Minor issues only. The map lacks the red, black and brown territory washes and blue hulls of 2.2, so the knuckles rest on plain terrain rather than 'the crowded inks'. Varma's brow is slightly knitted rather than fully level, but he is controlled, not heated. The rest is clean: V13 face with namam mark, pearl earrings, side knot toward his left, bare chest, gold necklaces and cream-and-gold cloth. His fist is on the map and his eyes are on Nagoji out of frame to the right. There is no text on the map, the anatomy is sound, and the wall, spear rack and rafters at upper left are clear for both balloons. The room matches 2.2.

Minor only: Nagoji wears a single dark leather riding gauntlet on his right hand (left forearm bare with the scar, consistent with the bible); the map is beige like 2.4 rather than the coloured territory washes of 2.2. Same hall, lighting and costumes as 2.4. Ramayyan sets the stylus across the palm-leaf bundle; Varma and Nagoji turn toward him. Map unlabelled, no painted text. Lettering fits on the laterite wall and spear rack above Ramayyan (RAMAYYAN), the rafters top right (VARMA) and the rafters top left or the table edge at the bottom (CAPTION).

Minor only. A faint stipple texture on the jaw reads as skin shading, not a beard, so the chin counts as clean-shaven. Varma's resting hand shows three fingers and a thumb, with the little finger tucked behind; that is plausible. The page shows the beat: Nagoji, eyes lowered, in close-up; Varma's hand with a gold bead bracelet and the gold-bordered cloth rests on an inked ring around the hill town; Ramayyan's palm-leaf bundles sit soft at the lower right; no other face is in frame. Nagoji matches his sheet: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, small flush gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. The hall matches panel 3.1: laterite wall, timber pillars, brass oil lamps and shuttered windows. There is no pseudo-text on the map. The plain laterite wall to the right of his head (about x 0.48 to 0.85, y 0.02 to 0.42) is clear space for both captions.

Minor only: the dark horse has a small white star (Kayal has none, but the script asks only for 'a dark horse' and the bible does not name Kayal for ch27). Nagoji's far boot shows beside the horse's chest because of the steep three-quarter view; it reads as his far leg, not a defect. The musketeers wear white head cloths, which the script allows. Laterite road, file of white-clad men with cross-belts and long guns, bullock carts and a steep-roofed Kerala palace on the far hill all match. No painted text. Open sky across the top for both captions.

Minor. The hilltop palace stands inside a low laterite compound wall with buttresses. The setting says no town walls or ramparts, but this reads as the palace compound and matches the palace in panel 3.3, so it is tolerated. De Lannoy wears white breeches and tall riding boots, not the mundu and sandals on his sheet. The chapter 24 to 27 bible row asks only for a white Travancore coat, and he has it: no red waistcoat, no blue coat, pale hair going grey, clean-shaven, a head taller than Nagoji. Nagoji matches his sheet: topknot, grey temples, thick moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. The scene has every script element: dusk; both officers on an earthen bund; the road blocked with felled palms; Nair sentries in white mundu with spears and matchlocks turning back a merchant cart; supply carts rolling along the bund; the old palace with a ring of siege fires below it. There is no text, blood or anachronism. Wide clear sky across the upper third holds both balloons, for example LANNOY at about x 0.25 to 0.45 and NAGOJI at about x 0.30 to 0.55, below LANNOY's.

Minor only. Varma's hair is black and bound into a low knot at the nape rather than the bible's side knot above the LEFT ear (his left side faces away, so the difference barely shows). Face, tilak, pearl drop earrings, bare chest and cream-and-gold cloth match the V13 sheet. The letter is a rolled tube with a cut cord and a red seal split in two. The map shows the hill town inside a full ring and has no writing. The lamps are brass with open wicks. The three captions fit in the dark rafter band across the top centre and right.

Acceptable. The over-the-shoulder framing works: Varma's profile is large in the right foreground, hand at his chin, eyes on nothing, bare-headed with his knot behind the visible left ear, pearl drop and gold beads. Nagoji sits level across the map table with topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. The pale forearm scar shows on his left forearm, his clasped hands are sound, and the map has no lettering. This is the same room and lighting as 4.2. Minor points: a faint wooden chair back shows behind Nagoji, and the table is chair-height rather than low with a floor mat. In 4.2 Nagoji stands, while here he is seated. Lettering: put Nagoji's short balloon in the roof band above his head (top left), and Varma's long balloon in the roof and pillar area at top centre (x 0.4 to 0.72, y 0 to 0.28), clear of both faces.

Clean. Revathi is alone at night on the verandah by a brass open-wick lamp. She matches her sheet and the chapter row: indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine in her braid, grey threading in her hair, flat-coin necklace, tali pendant, armlets and sandalwood lines. A tied palm-leaf letter, unopened, rests in her lap and her gaze is unfocused. Her hands are sound. The polished floor reflects the lamp but shows no rain. The caption fits on the plain wall above and left of her head or in the night sky at upper right.

Clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding curly hair, plain white cloth. He holds the stylus and palm-leaf bundle, eyes on the leaf, and no other face is in frame. The setting is the same night war hall with brass open-wick lamps, plain unlettered wall hangings and a map with no writing. His hands are sound. There is room for three balloons on the upper walls and rafters on both sides of his head. Varma speaks from off panel; his tail points to the left edge.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor: Savitri stands mid-hall facing Nagoji rather than at the far end of the hall as the script asks. The beat still reads clearly. Lettering space is limited to the dark door planks above and right of Nagoji's head and the ceiling and tan wall above and left of Savitri's head.

Minor only. Savitri wears a short-sleeved stitched blouse under the drape, which goes against the prompt's no-blouse line, though it matches her sheet and the neighbouring panels 5.2 and 6.1. Nagoji's jaw has faint shading that could read as light stubble, but the chin reads clean. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has the topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a gold stud, and the white coat with red waistcoat and silver chain, and he faces her level with his hands behind his back. Savitri stands square in front of him with a cold, thin smile, a lined face and grey-streaked hair in a low knot. Same hall and lighting as 5.2 and 5.3. Hands and anatomy are sound, with no text, blood or anachronism. There is clear dark space for both balloons: beams and pillar between the heads (x 0.43 to 0.58, y under 0.24) and the braced doors at top right (x 0.75 to 0.97, y under 0.19).
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor: the retainer has already laid hands on Nagoji's arm instead of reaching for a sword, but the beat still reads (retainer moves on Nagoji, Savitri halts him with a raised hand, Nagoji holds his ground, hands at his sides). The forearm brand and scar show as a healed pinkish scar, not a fresh wound. Nagoji's grey runs heavier than 'grey at the temples' but it matches the rest of the page. Same pillared hall, braced doors and lamps as 5.2. The dark carved ceiling and the door above Savitri's head give room for both lines.

Clean. The close two-shot matches the script: Nagoji has his topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin with light shading, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat and chain, and Savitri's eyes are on his. The carved frieze at top right is ornament, not pseudo-text. The dark doors at upper left and the ceiling above Savitri leave room for three balloons.

Clean. Savitri stands at the shrine doorway with her back half to camera, pinching up the wick of a tall open-wick brass lamp, with no glass chimney. Her grey-streaked low knot, lined face and plain white are all correct, and her hand is sound. The two background guards face away, so their faces do not read. The dark ceiling at top left and the plain reflective floor at bottom left are clear for both lines.

Clean. Nagoji is seen from inside the shrine doorway with the brass lamp flames large and out of focus in the left foreground and their glow on his brass buttons. He is quiet, with topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin with light shading, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. Savitri's off-panel line points to the left edge, where she stands by the lamp. The dark ceiling at top centre takes Nagoji's line, and the soft lamp blur at upper left takes hers.

Clean. Full-width low angle with Savitri facing front. She has her lean lined face, grey at the temples, low knot and plain white with no jewellery, and the shrine lamp glows behind her head. The hall, braced doors with the open wicket, and the guards stay consistent with the rest of the page. The dark ceiling at top left or the upper doors at top right take the single line clear of her face.

Minor. The script says 'alone', but two retainers with their backs turned stand in the background. This matches the room in 7.1. The fires beyond the window read more as a burning walled town than a ring of camp fires. Savitri's profile, low knot, grey streaks and plain white match the sheet. Same room and lighting as 7.1. No text. The ceiling and the upper window sky leave room for two balloons.

Follows the round-1 correction. It is a tight shot of Savitri still mounted, with her horse's ears and bridle at the bottom edge. She has a lean lined face, grey-streaked hair in a low knot at the nape, no jewellery and dusty white clothes, and her eyes lock on Nagoji, who is seen over the shoulder at right: long curly hair with grey, gold ear stud, moustache tip, white coat, red waistcoat collar. It matches 7.3 (palm banner, shrine, musketeers in white, smoke). No text, no blood. Grey sky above her head and across the top left gives room for the long caption. Minor: Nagoji's chain is drawn as silver beads rather than the heavy link chain in 7.3, and his topknot is cropped out of frame. The prompt's 'Nagoji outside the frame' note is overridden by the round-1 correction, which asked for this over-the-shoulder view.

All three round-1 faults are fixed. The trodden banner now carries the same palm-tree emblem as 7.3 and 7.4. There are no marks or pseudo-text in the corners. The small Dutch factors (dark coats, tricorns, walking canes) walk away along the canal road toward its vanishing point near the setting sun, so west into the palms. The evening field is emptied, with spears in the mud, an abandoned flintlock in the foreground and the shrine lamp in the palms. No bodies, blood, shore or sea. Open sunset sky across the upper left and centre holds both captions. Minor: the factors' navy coats with white breeches look a little like uniforms, but they carry canes, not arms.

Minor only. Savitri's drape leaves her right shoulder bare here, while 8.2 to 8.3 show a short-sleeved blouse. Nagoji's ear stud is tiny and reads pale or silver rather than gold. The guards wear white head cloths here but topknots in 8.2 and 8.3. Otherwise on-script: the open flap at sunset, the guards with spears, Savitri with bound wrists, bruise and dusty white clothes standing straight, Varma seated in turban and crest with his spear by the tent pole, and Nagoji to one side (topknot, grey temples, clean chin, dusty white coat, red waistcoat). Lettering: caption over the sky at top left, Varma's balloon in the tent cloth at top right.

Round-1 fault fixed: the stray bare-headed figure is gone. The only listener now is Marthanda Varma, seen from behind and out of focus at the right edge (cream-and-gold turban, peacock-feather crest, gold, cream-and-gold cloth), which matches 8.1. Minor issue: Savitri wears a short-sleeved stitched blouse under her drape, though the prompt asked for none. 8.3 shows the same blouse, so the page stays consistent. Everything else is on-script. She stands with her chin raised, the bruise on her RIGHT cheekbone (as in 8.1 and 8.3), grey-streaked hair in a low knot, wrists bound in front with coiled cord, and the hands are sound. The two Nair guards hold spears, the flap is open on the sunset field, and the brass lamp and red bolster are in place. There is no text. Lettering: her balloon fits the plain canopy at top right or the sky at upper left, clear of her face and hands.
Clean. Varma has risen and stands at arm's length facing Savitri (bound wrists, bruise, plain white). Both guards look at the ground. Same tent, open flap and sunset as 8.1. No lettering is needed.

Minor. Varma is seated on cushions again right after rising in 8.3. 8.5 and page 9 also show them seated, so it reads as the two sitting down after the silence. His expression is a furrowed sideways glance, closer to brooding than nostalgic, but acceptable for the weight of years. Savitri's profile at the right edge has the grey-streaked low knot. Lettering: two Varma balloons in the plain tent cloth between his turban and the centre pole, and at top left.

Round-1 fault fixed: Savitri's wrists are bound again with coiled rough cord, her hands resting in her lap, and the hands are sound. Remaining minor issue: in profile facing right, her bruise shows on her LEFT cheek, while 8.1 to 8.3 have it on the right. A reader could notice the flip, but it does not break the beat. She also wears the same short-sleeved blouse as 8.2 and 8.3. Otherwise strong. Savitri (left) and Varma (right) sit in close profile facing each other, and the seating follows 8.4. Varma's look matches his sheet: cream-and-gold turban with jewelled peacock crest, black hair, moustache, pearl earring, bare chest, gold necklaces and armlet. Nagoji is absent. The tent, lamp and open flap at sunset match the rest of the page, the guards outside are seen from behind, and there is no text. Lettering: wide plain tent canvas between and above the two heads (about x 0.35 to 0.52) and above the lamp at top left takes both balloons.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor: Savitri wears a short-sleeved stitched blouse. That matches her sheet and the page 8 frames, but the prompt asked for no blouse. The flags in the distance are plain white, while the banners in 9.1 are dark. Both are unlettered. Varma is off-panel to the right, where she is looking, so his tails go to the right edge.

Minor: Savitri wears a short-sleeved stitched blouse, the same as on her sheet and in the neighbouring panels. Varma speaks first but stands on the right, so the letterer should put his balloon at the top centre (tent ceiling) and Savitri's lower left in the sky.

Minor continuity: Savitri's hands are bound behind her back here, but in front in 9.3 and 9.4 (they are still visibly bound, as the script asks). Nagoji's silver chain of office hangs across the back of his white coat. He matches the chapter 27 row: topknot, grey at the temples, curled moustache, small gold ear stud, white coat with a red collar, no turban. All three lines are captions, so there are no tails.
